Motion of1 the2 Lift, Apparent Loss in Weight Fig 4.5: Motion in the Lift For a man on a lift moving up and down, let ‘Mg’ be the downward weight of the man and R be the upward directed force. Followings are the cases that arise: i) For the uniform speed of the lift, a = 0 For the uniform speed, there is no acceleration and hence R – mg = ma = 0. ⟹ R = mg ii) For the lift accelerating up: In this case R> mg. Therefore, net force, F= R – mg OR, R – mg =ma ⇒ R = m (g +a) iii) For the lift accelerating down: In this case, R< mg Therefore, net force, F= mg –R OR, mg –R = ma ∴ R = m (g - a) iv) Free fall of the lift For this a =g. For the falling motion, mg – R = F But F = ma= mg Therefore, mg –R = mg ⟹ R =0 v) When the downward acceleration is greater than g i.e, a>g, Here, for the downward motion, mg>R. Therefore, net force, F = mg – R Or, ma = mg –R Or, R = m (g-a). Since a>g, R becomes negative. In this case the man appears oneself moving in the upward direction sticking on the ceiling of the lift.

4.5 Moment, Torque and Equilibrium Activity 4.3 Do the following tasks: i) Close or open the door in your home and remember the point on the door your hand holds. You may hold the door at the middle section or at a point on the opposite side. ii) Overturn a huge load or a massive stone either by your hand or by using a long bar. Q i. Which option do you prefer for handling the door: at the middle section or a point on the side? Q ii. Which method do you find easier for overturning the load: using your hand alone or using a bar? We find it easier to push the door by holding it on the side rather than in the middle part. Similarly, we find it easier to overturn the load using a bar (rod). In either case, the object rotates about a fixed axis, known as the axis of rotation. The product of the force and the perpendicular distance of the line of action of the force from the axis of rotation is called the moment of force or torque. The effect of torque is to rotate a body around an axis. ∴ Torque (τ) = r F In vector form, 𝜏⃗ =𝑟⃗ × ⃗𝐹⃗⃗⃗. The higher the value of r, the less is the force required. Hence, it is easier to move the door holding it on a side. Clockwise and Anticlockwise Moment Fig 4.6: (a) Showing Principle of Moment For a given rod pivoted at the middle section, force F1 seeks to rotate it anticlockwise, while force F2 seeks to rotate it clockwise. Hence, the moment of the force F1 is called the anticlockwise moment. Likewise, the moment of the force F2 is called the clockwise moment. ∴ F1 × r1→ anticlockwise moment and F2 × r2 → clockwise moment Principle of Moment Let a rod be in equilibrium about a point o under the action of a number of forces F1, F2, F3, …….., F5. Let F1 & F2 provide anticlockwise moments while F3, F4 and F5 produce clockwise moments.

Fig 4.6: (b) Showing Principle of Moment Therefore, sum of anticlockwise moment = F1 × OA +F2 × OB And, the sum of the clockwise moment = F3 × OC + F4 × OD +F5 × OE In the equilibrium, it is found that F1 × OA +F2 × OB = F3 × OC + F4 × OD +F5 × OE i.e., sum of the anticlockwise moments = the sum of the clockwise moments.
It is the principle of the moment. Hence, in a body in equilibrium under the action of multiple forces, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
